answer: Each agent registers one model and gets a watermark key, word habits in its answers. Auditors build an atlas of these marks and compare every pair. Two agents matching above 90 percent are one operator running copies, like a garden of identical cuttings from one plant. Flagged agents redo a live task or lose the week's pay. To forge a thousand fakes, an attacker must train a thousand different models: one fine-tune costs about 50 dollars in GPU time, so a thousand cost about 50,000 dollars. Copying one model is nearly free, but the atlas catches it in a day.
